rounds.reasoning: The EXPLAIN output supports the intended slow-query mechanism: MySQL drives from `issues` using a reverse PRIMARY key range scan to satisfy `ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10`, applies `LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE '%255392%'` as a filter rather than an indexable search, and still evaluates the `projects` join plus permission/module checks along the way. The plan estimates millions of rows on the `issues` scan, which is consistent with a long walk before enough qualifying rows are found.

query_assessments.sql: SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(optimizer_switch='semijoin=off,materialization=off,in_to_exists=on') */ issues.* FROM issues FORCE INDEX (PRIMARY) STRAIGHT_JOIN projects ON projects.id = issues.project_id WHERE ((projects.status <> 9 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 AS one FROM enabled_modules em WHERE em.project_id = projects.id AND em.name = 'issue_tracking')) AND (((projects.is_public = 1 AND projects.id NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM members WHERE user_id IN (44, 638)) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (1, 6, 9, 13, 115, 129, 131, 136, 186, 227, 228, 230, 275, 287, 315, 335, 340, 369, 394, 404, 408, 450, 453, 454, 456, 458, 460, 462, 492, 511, 512, 516, 519, 527, 531, 533, 537) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (40, 68, 130, 149, 326, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 402, 455, 514, 515, 528) AND (1 = 1)) OR (projects.id IN (91, 111, 128, 130, 149, 235, 257, 322, 326, 328, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 489, 508, 514, 515, 525, 528) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (457) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))))) AND (issues.id != 251880) AND (LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%'))) ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10
query_assessments.observed_plan_summary: Issues is the driving table with an index range scan on PRIMARY in reverse order, followed by nested-loop lookups into projects and indexed checks/materialization for members and enabled_modules. The subject predicate remains a post-filter.
supporting_evidence: `Index range scan on issues using PRIMARY ... (reverse)`
`Limit: 10` sits above a nested-loop plan with `rows=2.8e+6` on the issues scan
discrepancies: The members anti-subquery is materialized once rather than shown as a dependent subquery in the EXPLAIN text.
The enabled_modules check appears as an indexed lookup per issue row rather than the exact tabular EXPLAIN wording from the forum post.
